questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to explore new cultures and study environment, to get away from my usual one. I was never really in doubt about going on exchange, since i think its a great opportunity to do get an great experience, while also studying.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, one of the greatest experiences ever. Met new friends, visited a lot of new cities and enjoyed it very much.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of information. We got a lot of mails and upon arrival, we talked to Massimo Costa, who helped us a lot with understanding everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We did not receive any assistance other than speaking to Massimo. We got all mails with the needed information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We found it quite easily, we booked through Spotahome, which had an apartment from the company Italianway. We already got our deposit back. 10/10 reccomendations

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it was great, to have my own place with my friends from Denmark

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It can be hard to understand at first, but i think people should know, that at UNIMIA you are guranteed your courses you apply for.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You first look at the courses, then you can se the schedule. If they overlap you can change or decide to be non-attending. It was very easy to navigate.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Massimo as always, but also articles. Overall, there website is quite easy to navigate and find appropriate courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all mine, as everybody else does when going on exchange at UNIMIA

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the classes and also the exam methods

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I actually found the level quite easy. The exams were kind of easy, but still learned a lot throughout the semester. I think they don´t take the exams as needing to be as difficult compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was honestly the same. Classes with a professor speaking and allowing for questions and elaborations if needed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Languages of the media
2. Digital society 
3. Human Resource Management
4. Corporate communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all of my courses
1. Languages of the media - American professor, who really enjoys learning people new things. Very sweet and always understanding
2. Digital society - same American professor, who really enjoys learning people new things. Very sweet and always understanding
3. Human Resource Management - Very easy exam, overall very italian professor and funny.
4. Corporate communication - Maybe the greatest class i have ever had. We really learned a lot and he was so sweet. The exam was harder compared to the others.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I mean, we traveled a lot, so hotels and rent of car. Overall, there were nothing unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I actually thought the supermarket would be cheaper, but many products such as meat, is almost the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not attend any, but read about a lot of them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend visiting a lot of the nearby cities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend visiting a lot of the nearby cities and experience the shopping life and bar life in Milano. I would recommend visting Parma, Florence, Venice, Piomente - Region for wine. And many more!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, they are very sweet and calm

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them, they are very open-minded.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I would say the relax way of approaching life, no stress. Just take it a day by day.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You are guaranteed your classes.
2. Enjoy every moment, it ends so quickly.
3. Have fun, experience a lot of things, don´t stay at home. Just keep doing something

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life, with new friends from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think it was the exam-period, balancing new friends with also studying. Overall studying was quite complicated due to the social culture of Italians

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: NO

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
